references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus uses exactly the same argument: "And if it is by Beelzebul that I cast out demons, by whom do your own sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges."
An example of Jewish exorcists who cast out evil spirits, supporting Jesus' point that "your own sons" also drove out demons.
The preceding accusation that Jesus cast out demons by Beelzebul, which is the context for Jesus' counterargument in verse 19.
Jesus' first argument against the accusation—that Satan would be divided against himself—which leads up to the further argument in verse 19.
The logical conclusion of the argument: If it is not by Beelzebul, but by the finger of God that Jesus casts out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon them.
The Pharisees' accusation in the Matthew parallel that Jesus casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of evil spirits, which sets the context for the counterargument.
